name: MathVista
description: MathVista is a consolidated Mathematical reasoning benchmark within Visual contexts. It consists of 6,141 examples derived from 28 existing multimodal datasets involving mathematics and 3 newly created datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, and PaperQA). The benchmark is designed to combine challenges from diverse mathematical and visual tasks, requiring fine-grained visual understanding and compositional reasoning.
creator: Pan Lu, Hritik Bansal, Tony Xia, Jiacheng Liu, Chunyuan Li, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Hao Cheng, Kai-Wei Chang, Michel Galley, Jianfeng Gao (UCLA, University of Washington, Microsoft Research)
publisher: UCLA, University of Washington, Microsoft Research

rai:dataCollection: MathVista incorporates 28 existing multimodal datasets, including 9 math-targeted question answering (MathQA) datasets and 19 VQA datasets. Three new datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, PaperQA) were created to address missing types of mathematical reasoning over specific visual contexts. IQTest comprises 228 examples requiring inductive reasoning, abstract thinking, pattern prediction, and calculations, sourced from puzzle test figures on online learning platforms. FunctionQA, with 400 examples, emphasizes subtle visual perceptions of functional plots and algebraic reasoning concerning variables, expressions, equations, and functions. PaperQA is a novel dataset featuring questions derived from informative academic illustrations, including tables, figures, and charts from online education resources, with 107 examples sourced from papers released in August 2023 on Huggingface.
rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Web Scraping, Document analysis
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Data was collected from 28 existing multimodal datasets (9 MathQA datasets and 19 VQA datasets) and 3 newly created datasets. For existing datasets, each source dataset was limited to up to 400 examples to ensure balanced representation. For VQA datasets, heuristic rules were used to automatically select examples likely to involve mathematical reasoning (examples with numeric answers or containing quantity words). For the three new datasets: IQTest was sourced from puzzle test figures on online learning platforms; FunctionQA emphasized functional plots and algebraic reasoning; PaperQA featured questions from academic illustrations in papers released in August 2023 on Huggingface.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For VQA datasets, automatic filtration using heuristic rules yielded 4,949 VQA-format examples. Three expert annotators manually labeled these examples to determine if they involve mathematical reasoning, using majority voting and limiting each source dataset to 400 examples, resulting in 2,739 examples. Each source dataset in MathVista was limited to up to 400 examples to ensure balanced representation. Examples are annotated with metadata including question type, answer type, task category, grade level, visual context, and required reasoning skills.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: All questions for the three new datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, PaperQA) were manually annotated by graduate students in STEM fields and further refined through a rigorous review process. A two-step annotation process was employed: initially, each dataset was independently annotated by three reviewers, resulting in a high inter-annotation consistency rate of 99.2%. Among the newly collected 736 questions, only 6 exhibited disagreements in the annotated answers. Discrepancies were resolved through discussion among the entire review team, ensuring consensus was reached on each example. For VQA datasets, three expert annotators manually labeled examples to determine if they involve mathematical reasoning, with detailed instructions provided. Annotators were trained using detailed instructions along with positive and negative examples. Three labeling options were provided: Yes (involves mathematical reasoning), No (does not involve mathematical reasoning), and Unsure (used sparingly). The Fleiss Kappa score for inter-annotator agreement was 0.775, indicating substantial consistency.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: A two-step annotation process was employed to ensure consistency. Initially, each dataset was independently annotated by three reviewers, resulting in a high inter-annotation consistency rate of 99.2%. Among the newly collected 736 questions, only 6 exhibited disagreements in the annotated answers. Discrepancies were resolved through discussion among the entire review team. For VQA dataset labeling, the Fleiss Kappa score was 0.775, indicating substantial inter-annotator agreement. For mathematical reasoning category labeling, 94.1% of examples from automatic and human annotations had the exact same set of reasoning types, while 98.79% of individual labels were identical, indicating high accuracy of automatic annotation.
rai:annotatorDemographics: Graduate students in STEM fields annotated the three new datasets. For human performance baseline evaluation, annotators from Amazon Mechanical Turk were required to have a satisfactory annotating history, successfully pass qualification examples, and possess a high school degree or higher.
rai:dataLimitations: While MathVista encompasses a broad spectrum of tasks and visual contexts, there may be gaps in the representation of certain types of mathematical problems and visuals. The dataset's focus on mathematical reasoning within visual contexts, spanning specific domains like science and college-level math, necessitates a more labor-intensive process for collecting high-quality data compared to textual-only or general-purpose datasets. Annotations were sourced from original data providers, resulting in only 85.6% of examples having annotations. Due to the heterogeneity of these sources, annotations lack a unified format and structure. The scalability and generalizability of the benchmark to other domains remain a concern.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset was primarily designed for use as a test set to evaluate mathematical reasoning capabilities of foundation models in visual contexts. It can be used commercially as a test set, but using it as a training set is prohibited. The benchmark facilitates the development of mathematical reasoning systems in visually intensive scenarios and evaluates research progress of LLMs and LMMs, especially their capabilities in solving rigorous reasoning tasks.
